Then make scene.klad and paint a night scene: a hooded traveller holding a lantern out to a ruined arch, a small creature following, flat shaded and lit by the lantern. Give your agent real brushes. klad is a 2D painting and animation app you share with a coding agent. You paint in the editor with a pen. The agent paints through the klad command line, with the same brushes, on the same drawing, and each of you sees the other's strokes instantly. don't want to build it? Sign up for the pre-built app release at klad.studio There is no image model in klad. Your agent (Claude Code, Codex, anything that can run commands) decides what to paint; klad gives it brushes, layers and a timeline. Whatever either of you puts down stays what it was: a stroke with its path, pressure, brush and colour, a shape with its points, a fill with its region. So there's no rerolling and hoping for the best: if one leaf looks off, you fix that leaf. Asked for "a little sprout creature for my game", the agent paints 4,344 strokes and fills. You change them: recolour the leaves, bend the mouth, move a smudge, blend the blush. Then the agent animates it: the creature's parts go into five groups, 205 keys move them, and no frame is painted again. Drawings made with Claude Fable 5.2: the creature, the scene and the prop kit were painted stroke by stroke through the klad command line. An image generator hands you pixels, and the only edit left is another roll of the dice. klad keeps every stroke and every fill as data: where it went, how hard it was pressed, its brush and its colour. Pick any of them hours later, yours or the agent's, and recolour it, bend it, move it or delete it. The prompt to start with is under Try it . klad skill prints the agent skill in docs/skill/SKILL.md : how to look at a drawing, change it and check the result. A second one, klad skill drawing ( docs/skill/drawing/SKILL.md ), teaches the craft: planning a picture, light on form, values, edges, colour, materials and how to judge the result. Both are MIT, so use them with any agent and any tool. Open the drawing to watch and draw along: What an agent paints depends on the agent and on how much you steer it. The skills teach it the tool and some craft; the pen in your hand does the rest. Everything you can do in the editor has a klad command too, so a script or an agent works on the same drawing you have open. It reads strokes as JSON, changes any of them by its address and applies batches of edits as JSON ops. The file format is documented down to the byte under the MIT licence ( docs/format.md ), so other apps and engines can read and write klad drawings with or without klad. Props, characters, backgrounds and frame-by-frame animation. Draw the key poses and klad makes the drawings in between, part by part; it checks the arcs (a foot that slides, a part that sinks under the ground), colours every drawing from the first one, and exports sprite sheets or a Godot SpriteFrames scene with each clip's timing. klad inbetween creature.klad --layers lines,colour --from 3 --to 5 --spacing in-out klad arcs creature.klad --track ' lines:near leg ' --clip walk --check klad export creature.klad --godot ../game/art Try it git clone https://github.com/klad-app/klad && cd klad just compile # about ten minutes the first time target/release/klad open # on Linux: target/linux/release/klad open Then let your agent paint Put klad on your path, for you and for your agent: target/release/klad install (on Linux target/linux/release/klad install ; on a Mac it may ask for your password). Start your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, or anything else that can run commands) in the folder where the drawing should go, and paste: Run klad skill and klad skill drawing and read what they print. Then make scene.klad and paint a night scene: a hooded traveller holding a lantern out to a ruined arch, a small creature following, flat shaded and lit by the lantern. Once it has made scene.klad , open it in another terminal to watch the strokes land, and draw along: klad open scene.klad . Then steer it. Press N to pin a note on the canvas ("more moss on this side") and tell the agent to read your notes, or pick any stroke with S and change it yourself. Every build holds the klad command line tool, the editor, the fonts, the licences, the agent skill and six sample drawings to look at and draw on (the start window shows them; klad samples lists them and copies one out). The first start offers first steps: draw a shape, fill it and hand the drawing to an agent. The guides in docs/guide/ show how to paint, select, fill, animate, rig and export in the editor, one recipe at a time, starting with Getting started . Building takes about ten minutes the first time. just build # release build of the klad CLI and the editor just test # every test, and the drawkit check just lint # rustfmt and clippy, warnings as errors just audit # licences, RustSec advisories, sources, and the notices are current just samples # build the sample drawings Licence klad is source-available, not open source, copyright Indicode BV. klad is built on open source libraries, fonts and Skia; their licences are in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md , also shown by klad licences and in the editor's About window.
